summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with shortness of breath, right-sided pleuritic chest pain, and left leg pain. Due to an elevated D-dimer and inability to perform a CT scan on admission because of a prior contrast allergy, she was started on a heparin drip empirically. Bilateral leg ultrasounds showed no DVT, and after premedication, a CT angiogram ruled out pulmonary embolism. The chest pain was attributed to a small right pleural effusion and mild atelectasis, with possible contribution from volume overload. She developed a mild, stable rash post-contrast despite premedication, managed with antihistamines. Her left knee pain, related to a prior tibial fracture, was stable on imaging; the brace was confirmed to fit appropriately. Her HIV remained well-controlled, and liver findings were consistent with chronic hepatitis B and C with fatty infiltration. She improved clinically, was weaned to baseline oxygen, and discharged home on her prior medications with instructions to follow up for rash resolution and orthopedic care.
